alt: A list has its first value removed with pop(0). The removed cell becomes an empty gap, and every later value moves one slot left, one step at a time, until the gap leaves the end of the list. A second list has its last value removed with pop(), and nothing moves. Presets use lists of four values and of two values.

steps.caption: front = [10, 20, 30, 40]. `front.pop(0)` removes the value at index 0, which is 10.
10 is gone, so index 0 is empty. A list has no gaps, so Python closes it by moving every later value one slot left.
20 moves from index 1 to index 0. The empty slot is now at index 1.
30 moves from index 2 to index 1. The empty slot is now at index 2.
40 moves from index 3 to index 2. That was the last move: `pop(0)` moved 3 values, and the cell at index 3 leaves the list.
Now `front` is [20, 30, 40]. One `pop(0)` on a list of 4 values cost 3 moves, and a longer list costs more.
back = [10, 20, 30, 40]. `back.pop()` with no index removes the last value, 40, at index 3.
Now `back` is [10, 20, 30]. Nothing sits after the removed value, so no value moved and every other index stayed the same.
front = [7, 9]. `front.pop(0)` removes the value at index 0, which is 7.
7 is gone, so index 0 is empty. A list has no gaps, so Python closes it by moving every later value one slot left.
9 moves from index 1 to index 0. That was the last move: `pop(0)` moved 1 value, and the cell at index 1 leaves the list.
Now `front` is [9]. One `pop(0)` on a list of 2 values cost 1 move, and a longer list costs more.
back = [7, 9]. `back.pop()` with no index removes the last value, 9, at index 1.
Now `back` is [7]. Nothing sits after the removed value, so no value moved and every other index stayed the same.
